title: U.S. House · Texas's 25th Congressional District
area: North-central Texas, spanning from Tarrant County (Fort Worth area) north into rural counties along I-35.

context.text: Texas redrew its congressional district boundaries in August 2025 ahead of the 2026 elections, a mid-decade redistricting.
In the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary, Dione Sims defeated William Marks, 60.5% to 39.5%. Roger Williams was unopposed in the Republican primary.

summary.text: Roger Williams is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Texas's 25th District. A former baseball player, small-business owner and Texas Secretary of State (2005–2007), he was first elected to Congress in 2012 and chairs the House Committee on Small Business. He is also a member of the Financial Services Committee.

background.text: Born in Evanston, Illinois, in 1949, and raised in Fort Worth, Texas, according to Ballotpedia and his official biography.
Earned a bachelor's degree in education from Texas Christian University in 1972. His official biography says he was an All-Southwest Conference baseball player at TCU.

Played baseball in the Atlanta Braves farm system, then worked as a small business owner and baseball coach. His 2020 campaign website said he had been a small business owner in Texas for over 45 years.

Began his political involvement in 1994 as a fundraiser for then-Governor George W. Bush and was North Texas Finance Chairman for the 2000 Bush/Cheney presidential campaign, according to his official biography. His 2020 campaign website also said President Bush appointed him in 2001 as chairman of the Republican National Finance Committee's Eagles Program.
Served as Texas Secretary of State from 2005 to 2007; his official biography says he also served as the state's chief liaison for the Texas border and Mexican affairs.
First elected to the U.S. House in 2012 and represents a district stretching from Tarrant County in the east to Callahan County in the west.
Currently chairs the House Committee on Small Business and serves on the House Financial Services Committee.

His official biography lists bills he worked on that passed the House, including the Assisting Small Businesses Not Fraudsters Act, the Main Street Parity Act and the Strengthening Oversight of Iran's Access to Finance Act.

Serves on the TCU Board of Trustees; his 2020 campaign website also listed service on the board of the Bush School of Government and Public Service at Texas A&M University. His official biography says he lives in Weatherford, Texas, and has two daughters and grandchildren.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Financial Services and chairs the House Committee on Small Business in the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Dione Sims
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 60.5% of the vote

summary.text: Dione Sims is a software quality development director, community organizer and nonprofit founder who won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 60.5% of the vote. She describes herself as a granddaughter of Dr. Opal Lee and says she is running on living wages, public schools and an economy that works for working people.

background.text: Graduated from Southwest High School and earned a bachelor's degree from Texas Wesleyan University in 1989, according to Ballotpedia.
Works in information technology; in her Candidate Connection survey she describes herself as a software quality development director who has led diverse teams of professionals.
Describes herself as the president and founder of a nonprofit focused on unity, understanding and social justice.

Describes herself as the granddaughter of Dr. Opal Lee, whom she calls the Grandmother of Juneteenth. Says she has co-produced the Annual Juneteenth Fort Worth Celebration since 2015 and helped lead the Opal's Walk campaign for national Juneteenth recognition.
Says she has served on several boards, and lists endorsements from Fort Worth officials and the Fort Worth Association of Federated Women's Club.
Defeated William Marks in the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary, 60.5% to 39.5%, to become the party's nominee against Rep. Williams.

priorities.text: In her 2026 Ballotpedia survey, said she is passionate about protecting democracy, expanding access to affordable healthcare, economic dignity for working families, criminal justice reform, mental health, and civil and human rights.
Said she is running to help Congress 'reclaim its constitutional role' and restore checks and balances against unchecked executive power.
Said she would fight for living wages, strong public schools, and an economy that works for working people.

positions.summary: Says she is passionate about expanding access to affordable healthcare.
Says she would fight for living wages for working people.
